sources.entry: Cortex - Generates API documentation, typed SDKs, and MCP servers from API specifications and Markdown. #free #opensource

summary.one_liner: Cortex is a toolchain that turns OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, GraphQL, gRPC (Protocol Buffer), OpenRPC, and Markdown sources into typed SDKs, interactive documentation, and an MCP server for AI agents, all from one project configuration.
summary.what_it_does: Reads API specifications and Markdown pages declared in a cortex.config.yml file and generates client SDKs in many languages (TypeScript, Python, Go, Java, Kotlin, Ruby, PHP, C#, Rust, C++, C). It builds static HTML documentation with interactive API reference pages and can export it for static hosting. It also generates an MCP server with typed tools, embedded specifications, SDK guides, and project docs for AI agents. A CLI validates configs, supports dry-run generation, and publishes generated packages to registries and GitHub. The README also describes a free hosted deploy to a cortexdocs.dev subdomain for public GitHub repositories.
use_cases: generate typed API client SDKs from OpenAPI specs
give AI agents access to API docs via MCP
combine multiple API specs into one SDK
host documentation from a Git repository
document WebSocket, GraphQL, gRPC, or JSON-RPC APIs
notable: One YAML project config drives SDKs, docs, and MCP server generation
Supports OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, GraphQL, gRPC, OpenRPC, and Markdown in one project
Generated MCP server embeds specs and exposes .proto files as resources
Sparse Eta template overrides for customizing output
Free hosted docs deploy for public GitHub repositories via npx
caveats: Deploy requires repository write access; MCP works with public read access
Some generated SDKs require the target language's compiler or package manager
The generated MCP server does not call gRPC methods; it only exposes .proto files as resources
Requires Node.js 20 or later and npm 10 or later
